name: Question 6
worked_solution:
Since we have $\,T({b}_{1})={b}_{1}-{b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}\,$, we have

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and let T:R2→R2 be a linear transformation. Find [T]B if T(b1)=b2−2b2+b1 and T(b2)=3b2+2b1−5b2.

a
[13−221−5]
b
[1−2132−5]
c
[1−12−2]
d
[12−1−3]
e
[12−1−2]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have T(b1)=b1−b2 and T(b2)=2b1−2b2, we have [T(b1)]B=[1−1],[T(b2)]B=[2−2]. Now, the B-matrix for T is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1) and T(b2) relative to the basis B. Therefore, we obtain [T]B=[12−1−2].
